a22.speaker: Adama Barrow, President of The Gambia
a22.speech: Extended sympathy to the Carter family, the American Government, and the world, for the loss of Jimmy Carter, and referred to Carter as a great president and a great human being. "I think what he has achieved after his presidency was great, and he spent his entire life supporting humanity. He was very social and I think this is an encouragement for all presidents that there is life after the presidency." Expressed his profound sadness, adding that Carter has achieved a lot that they should remember him for.

a166.speaker: Pavel Bílek, Czech Ambassador to Ghana
a166.speech: Commended the Bone Marrow Transplant and Stem Cell Centre initiative as a major step in specialised healthcare in the country. ; Explained that the donation formed part of an ongoing collaboration between the Czech Republic and local healthcare stakeholders aimed at strengthening Ghana's medical infrastructure and infection control systems, and added that Czechia had been involved in Ghana's development since its independence. ; Said the Czech branch of the Austrian company, VAMED, handed over 22 fully equipped hospitals to Ghana, and stated that 12 of these facilities began operations earlier this year, funded by Czech and Austrian banks. ; Acknowledged the vital contributions of Czech doctors, who have provided free surgical services to thousands of Ghanaian patients as part of the MEDEVAC programme. ; Expressed gratitude to SEDA Africa Group for its role in assisting the hospital and reiterated his commitment to improving healthcare in the country through such gestures.

a166.speaker: Dr Leslie Issa Adam-Zakaria, Medical Director of the Greater Accra Regional Hospital
a166.speech: Expressed gratitude to the Czech Republic for the support. ; Said the hospital usually provided services to people who could not afford the services offered by the hospital, and as a result did not receive the true value of the services offered, making it difficult to run the facility. ; Said the partnership would go a long way to not only sterilise delicate equipment and increase their lifespan but to improve service delivery at the hospital, and stressed the hospital's commitment to improving healthcare quality for all.

a202.speaker: T.E. Dovgalenko, Director of the Department of Partnership with Africa of the Russian Foreign Ministry
a202.speech: On the department's main areas of work: “Our task is to develop comprehensive relations with Africa and strengthen their truly strategic character. Today it is a dynamically developing continent. It is not only and not so much about the huge natural resources that are the key to the economic sovereignty of African countries, but also about the colossal human capital.” ; Building relations with the African Union, as well as regional and sub-regional associations of the continent, alliances of states, multilateral formats and mechanisms is another key area of the department's work.

a202.speaker: T.E. Dovgalenko, Director of the Department of Partnership with Africa of the Russian Foreign Ministry
a202.speech: On the impetus for Russian-African relations: “In recent years, Russian-African cooperation has reached a qualitatively new level. The first and second Russia–Africa summits, as well as the first ministerial conference of the Russia–Africa Partnership Forum last November, provided a powerful impetus for this. Together with our African friends, we are working on the practical implementation of the agreements reached, based on the Action Plan adopted at the summit in St. Petersburg.”

a202.speaker: T.E. Dovgalenko, Director of the Department of Partnership with Africa of the Russian Foreign Ministry
a202.speech: On trade: “The volume of trade and economic cooperation, which reached a record high of $24.5 billion in 2023, continues to grow. Work is underway on the implementation of major investment projects on the continent, including in the fields of energy, the creation of transport and logistics chains, the formation of a system of secure mutual settlements, high technologies, including space exploration and digital technologies.”

a202.speaker: T.E. Dovgalenko, Director of the Department of Partnership with Africa of the Russian Foreign Ministry
a202.speech: On the Sahel States Alliance: “The creation of the Sahel States Alliance Confederation is an important step in consolidating the efforts of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger to ensure national security and address socio-economic challenges. The most important goal of the association is to counter the terrorist threat in the Sahara-Sahel zone. The situation in the region is really difficult, including with the help of the West, which was directly involved in the destruction of Libyan statehood in 2011. Russia provides assistance both in strengthening counter-terrorism capabilities and increasing the combat capability of the national armed forces by sending military specialists and equipment, training military personnel and law enforcement officers, and in the socio-economic development of the countries of the region.”

a202.speaker: T.E. Dovgalenko, Director of the Department of Partnership with Africa of the Russian Foreign Ministry
a202.speech: On food aid: “Our country provides humanitarian assistance to the needy population of African countries both through bilateral channels and through international organizations. The United Nations World Food Program is a key multilateral channel for us to provide such assistance. The Russian government has allocated the necessary financing to the program for the supply of domestic food to Zambia, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger and Sudan. However, due to the sanctions imposed by Washington in November 2024 against Russian financial institutions, funds have not been transferred yet.”

a202.speaker: T.E. Dovgalenko, Director of the Department of Partnership with Africa of the Russian Foreign Ministry
a202.speech: On education cooperation: “We give priority attention to the issues of training highly qualified personnel among Africans, who are called upon to ensure, among other things, the economic and technological sovereignty of their countries. More than 34,000 African students study in Russia, of which about seven thousand are funded by the federal budget.”

a308.speaker: Michael Buerk, BBC journalist
a308.speech: "Dawn. And as the sun breaks through the piercing chill of night on the plain outside Korem it lights up a biblical famine, now in the 20th century. This place, say workers here, is the closest thing to hell on earth."

a308.speaker: Michael Buerk, BBC journalist
a308.speech: Would later say his report was "one of the most influential pieces of television ever broadcast".

a308.speaker: The film makers of the BBC television movie "When Harvey met Bob"
a308.speech: Describe the television movie as "humorous, warm, tension-filled and ultimately deeply moving."

a308.speaker: Bob Geldof, musician and Live Aid organiser (writing in The Sun)
a308.speech: Told the people of England to be proud because they had led the fight to help the world's poorest for more than 25 years; said the UK can claim credit for cancelling the debt borne by the "poorest of the poor", for sending 42 million children to school for the first time and for ensuring 3.8 million "of the poorest, most ill people in the world get free medicine" ; "This country's word is its bond. See, we can change things if we put our mind to it. At least for some people. At least for the most vulnerable and hurt in our world. We can do that. We proved it. Well done us."

a308.speaker: CIA documents and a BBC investigation
a308.speech: Showed LiveAid money had been channelled to buy arms for anti-government rebel forces and that this further fuelled the very humanitarian crisis the charity was supposed to stem.

a308.speaker: Simon Anholt, expert on national identity and nations' brands, creator of the Anholt-GfK Roper Nation Brands Index
a308.speech: Said Geldof's relentless depiction of Africa as a single, hopeless basket case had harmed the long-term development prospects of the entire continent: "I have often commented about the unintended damage done to the international standing and, consequently, the long-term prospects of poorer countries by well-intentioned charity promotion, and in particular the negative 'branding' of Africa by aid celebrities like Geldof and Bono" ; "In order to continue to assist poorer countries, donors feel it necessary to paint as distressed a picture as they can of the recipient: Donor governments need to maintain the support of domestic taxpayers by persuading them the cause is worthy, while charities and other NGOs need to keep up the level of voluntary donations. The more desperate they make the country appear, the more successful their programmes will become." ; "Using their vast credibility, resources and media influence, donors project onto the public imagination an unbroken stream of corrosively negative information, images and emotions about the recipient country and its population, to prove that no cause is more heart-rending, more urgent, and more (nearly) hopeless. By the time their programme has moved on to the next deserving cause, the country's image may have been blighted for generations, leaving a powerful psychological and emotional disincentive to trade, investment, tourism and growth."

a308.speaker: Simon Anholt, expert on national identity and nations' brands
a308.speech: Maintains that foreign aid mechanisms corrode the economies of recipient countries making it impossible for local producers to compete equally and fairly against a steady stream of free food, goods and money: "What we have failed to notice is how it also makes pariahs of those countries in international public opinion, stealing their dignity as proper states with history, culture, nature, wisdom, language, learning and human endeavour by branding them as nothing more than victims and beggars for decades to come. Instead of images of natural and human beauty and variety, the 'outside world' is fed an unvarying diet of conflict, starvation, disease and despair; a world of dust and misery. Nothing could be more unhelpful for a country that needs to build an economy through the stimulation of trade, tourism, investment and productive cultural and political relations with other states."

a1108.speaker: Vimbainashe Chakanungwa, mother of patient Gracious Chikova
a1108.speech: "I had given up. Those with money have been taking their children to India for surgery, but I simply could not afford it," said Vimbainashe Chakanungwa as she helped her daughter sip her meal.

a1108.speaker: Vimbainashe Chakanungwa, mother of patient Gracious Chikova
a1108.speech: "I had resorted to prayer, just hoping for a miracle." ; "It is impossible to open my heart to show my gratitude and happiness. I was afraid that I could lose my baby, but here is the baby. She is back to life."

a1108.speaker: Kudzai Kanyepi, Zimbabwe's first and only female heart surgeon
a1108.speech: "There is no medication that can replace surgery. The burden of disease remains, and unfortunately some of the children pass away without getting the help they desperately need." ; "It is the reason why we continue to work in our country. There is nothing greater than helping your own people."

a1108.speaker: US Centres for Disease Control and Prevention
a1108.speech: According to the US CDC, globally about one in every 100 children is born with congenital heart disease, making it the world's most common birth defect.

a1108.speaker: Simukayi Machawira, head of cardiology at Parirenyatwa hospital
a1108.speech: Said an estimated 4,500 children in Zimbabwe are born with heart disease each year, with many unable to access surgery, and that of those, 30 percent — or around 1,200 infants — are likely to die in their first year if untreated ; "You can imagine, it's quite a lot of children."

a1108.speaker: Hesham Shawky, Egyptian surgical team leader
a1108.speech: "This is the only solution for many people in Africa because they can't afford private care," he said.

a1314.speaker: Wesley Macheso, Head of the Department of Literary Studies at the University of Malawi (Unima)
a1314.speech: On what motivated him to venture into creative writing: “To me, creative writing is an art that mostly emerges from talent. So, I believe I always had that talent in me only that I had to unleash it through practice. Having said that, I cannot downplay the influence of the environment I grew up in. We always had a lot of books and my parents were always reading and encouraging us to read. So, it may be those stories I read as a child that influenced me to write.”

a1314.speaker: Wesley Macheso, Head of the Department of Literary Studies at the University of Malawi (Unima)
a1314.speech: On his success stories: “Writing has been a blessing to me. I have travelled to several countries around the world because I am a writer. Apart from travelling and attending writing workshops and seminars, writing has also earned me international recognition. I have so far published two books and several short stories in international anthologies and online magazines.” He cites being a writer in residence at the University of Iowa's International Writing Program (IWP), participating in the Miles Morland Foundation creative writing workshop, being three times shortlisted for the Morland scholarship, winning the Peer Gynt Literary Award for his novella Akuzike and the Gods, being shortlisted for the Short Story Day Africa prize, and participating in the African Writers' Trust editing and publishing training workshop: “All these, and more, have helped improve my art to serve writing better.”

a1314.speaker: Wesley Macheso, Head of the Department of Literary Studies at the University of Malawi (Unima)
a1314.speech: On the state of creative writing in Malawi: “I think, as a country, we are getting back on our feet in terms of writing. I am saying this because there is a noticeable gap in creative output when you compare with the 80s and 90s to the first decade of the 21st century. Maybe it was the frenzy of democracy, or something else, but the good thing is that we are seeing more new Malawian voices emerging. The Malawi Writers Union (Mawu) has also risen from the grave and the future looks very promising.”

a1314.speaker: Wesley Macheso, Head of the Department of Literary Studies at the University of Malawi (Unima)
a1314.speech: On what is not being done right: “What we are doing better is that we are trying to write, but I think we are still failing to set the right standards for our writing. Most of the new generation writers show lack of awareness on what writing and publishing is all about. You will find a lot of people self-publishing, which to me, is a weakness. A writer must go through the rigorous process of submitting their work to accredited publishers for peer review, the same way iron goes through fire. Vanity publishing will not take us anywhere and that is why there are very few Malawian names on the international stage. We must refuse to be mediocre.”

a1314.speaker: Wesley Macheso, Head of the Department of Literary Studies at the University of Malawi (Unima)
a1314.speech: On the Department of Literary Studies and shaping creative writers: “As a university, and especially under our department, we have nurtured writing for a very long time. The story of writing in Malawi cannot be complete without mentioning the Writers' Workshop at the then Chancellor College. This workshop still exists. Most of our big names like Jack Mapanje, Ken Lipenga and Steve Chimombo are products of that workshop. Today, the Department of Literary Studies offers courses in creative writing; from fiction, poetry, to creative non-fiction. These courses are offered in the Bachelor of Arts (Literary and Cultural Studies) programme. We also have plans to introduce a degree programme in Literature and Creative Writing, which should see us shaping more creative writers.”

a1314.speaker: Wesley Macheso, Head of the Department of Literary Studies at the University of Malawi (Unima)
a1314.speech: On the digital world and technology: “I believe that good writing is known by its affinity to humanity. The human element must be there and that is why writing generated by new technologies like Artificial Intelligence (AI) will never beat original creativity. In short, writers must write and not rely too much on technology for creativity. On the other hand, we must learn to use digital platforms like e-zines and blogs to expose our work. Social media platforms are also useful as a lot of opportunities are shared there, and we can take advantage of such openings to sell our work internationally. We actually need a Malawian digital magazine worth its salt out there!”

a1314.speaker: Wesley Macheso, Head of the Department of Literary Studies at the University of Malawi (Unima)
a1314.speech: Advice to creative writers: “My advice to writers is that they must write and they must read. The only way one can improve their art is through practice, and for writing, practicing means reading and writing. As a university department that is entirely into the teaching of literature, we are in need of more Malawian voices. We would love to see more properly published work by Malawians that we can incorporate into our curriculum.” ; “I just want to remind writers out there that writing is very rewarding, but it demands patience and meticulosity. There are certain habits one has to cultivate first before they call themselves a writer. I am still learning, myself, but eventually it will happen.”

a1524.speaker: Balarabe Lawal, Minister of Environment of Nigeria
a1524.speech: Has solicited the support of the African Development Bank (AfDB) in funding the National Agency for the Great Green Wall (NAGGW) ; "I want to appeal for the extension of your support to Nigeria's National Agency for Great Green Wall. The agency is responsible for fencing the Sahelian part of Africa to prevent desertification. I also want to plead that you should look at what we have done so far in trying to address environmental degradation in the 11 frontline States in Nigeria. We have already submitted our proposal to the Ministry of Finance on the issue of clean cooking policy, which is also directly linked to the afforestation process. That, also, is important because it is trying to address two issues of deforestation and health. When you go to the rural areas, most women cook with firewood, and that often exposes them to health issues, and even affects the children."

a1524.speaker: News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
a1524.speech: Reports that the meeting was at the instance of Vice President Kashim Shettima; that the agency was established to address land degradation and desertification, boost food security, and support communities in adapting to climate change in Sokoto, Kebbi, Katsina, Zamfara, Kano, Jigawa, Bauchi, Gombe, Yobe, Borno, and Adamawa; and that SAPZ Phase Two is expected to scale up climate-resilient infrastructure and inclusive agro-industrial growth across an additional 24 states.

a1524.speaker: Ahmed Dangiwa, Minister of Housing and Urban Development of Nigeria
a1524.speech: Appealed to the AfDB boss to support the ministry in addressing the housing deficit, adding that the housing sub-sector needed a lot of funding ; "We want your intervention in terms of construction of housing development in Nigeria. Because there is a very high return on investment in Nigeria if you are investing in agric, health, and education. Housing is key sector to draw up a framework to ensure that you fund affordable housing for the population of the country."

a1524.speaker: Sidi Ould Tah, President of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a1524.speech: Assured that under his leadership he would waste no effort in making the bank provide Nigeria with the support it deserves in terms of developing its human capital ; "My vision for the bank is not a lending institution, it is a catalyst institution with which to mobilise resources, capital from all over the world to bring. I hope we can really bring capital to the continent to make transformation of our continent and bring value to the agricultural sector. This is why my four cardinal points are: mobilise large-scale capital through partnerships, reforming Africa's financial architecture, converting the continent's demographic dividend into economic strength for job creation. These points form my roadmap to guide the bank's strategy and accelerate Africa's development, and I'm confident that with your support, the bank will be able to bring transformation to the continent."

a1524.speaker: Kashim Shettima, Vice President of Nigeria
a1524.speech: Requested AfDB support for the funding of phase two of the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones (SAPZ); averred that Nigeria was the largest shareholder in AfDB, while the country's portfolio hovers in the neighbourhood of over $10 billion ; "We urge you to further support us in the phase 2 Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones (SAPZ). You assisted us with $300 million when you were in Liberia. We want to thank you, but, like Oliver Twist, we are asking for more because we are poised to diversify our mono-product economy into agriculture, especially value-added agricultural exports. And we have the potential, with all due respect, your Excellency, in all the agro-ecological zones in Nigeria. From the mangrove swamps forest in the South to the Sahelian region in the far North, you can virtually grow anything. In states like Kebbi, you can plant money, and if money can grow, it shows that the soil is fertile."

a1524.speaker: Kashim Shettima, Vice President of Nigeria
a1524.speech: Pointed to the relationship between the economy and ecology in the Sahel region: "We are from the same part of the world, essentially same terrain, same geography, and same challenges, especially challenges of armed banditry and extremism. So, we want to solicit your support; our doors are ever open."

a1524.speaker: Kashim Shettima, Vice President of Nigeria
a1524.speech: Asserted that Nigeria was hungry for development because Nigerian youths were eager to be co-opted into the workforce of the 21st century, and assured that young Nigerians have the entrepreneurial zeal and passion enough to be captured in that workforce; implored the AfDB chief to also look into the issue of the bank's support for innovation-driven enterprises, instead of only MSMEs, saying the digital space offered a vista of opportunity for Africa's development ; "And we can catalyse and accelerate the digital space in Africa for Nigeria, and we can have deep tech enterprises to come out of Africa. Of the eight unicorns in Africa, five are from Nigeria - Moniepoint, Jummia, and the rest. We want to once again reiterate that we are with you, we are for you, and we will stand by you."

a1524.speaker: Kashim Shettima, Vice President of Nigeria
a1524.speech: Assured Mr Drew that President Bola Tinubu was determined to rekindle friendship and brotherhood between both nations ; "Going forward, we should have a robust engagement and understanding. We should stand by each other. We should stand for one another. We should stand on each other's interests. For St. Kitts and Nevis, and Nigeria, what binds us together supersedes whatever divides us. Majority of the population of the Caribbean are of African descent. A chunk of them are English-speaking countries. Quite a large number of them belong to the Commonwealth. So, the commonalities we share are so high, but contact has been low, relative to what it ought to be. So, your Excellency, I want to assure you that my boss is very kin in rekindling that friendship, that sense of brotherhood and sisterhood, and see to it that going forward, we should have a robust engagement and understanding." ; He further recalled that Tinubu was in Saint Lucia earlier in the year as part of his broader package of reaching out to the Caribbean Africans in diaspora: "The president had also established contact with our brothers in Brazil. The largest African population in the world outside of Nigeria is found in Brazil."

a1524.speaker: Terrance Drew, Prime Minister of St. Kitts and Nevis
a1524.speech: Decried the low level of trade and contact between Caribbean countries and Africa, and expressed the country's readiness to work closely with the Nigerian Government to boost trade on the African continent.

a1899.speaker: INGOs (joint statement)
a1899.speech: Sound alarm on imminent atrocities in Al Fasher, call for urgent protection of civilians. Say markets, hospitals, mosques, and displacement camps have been repeatedly targeted, leaving families without food, medicine, or safe shelter; that civilians attempting to flee face extortion, ethnic targeting, sexual violence, and killings along the routes, while prohibitive costs make escape impossible for most; that local responders and aid workers are under attack as they struggle to sustain communal kitchens and basic care; and that local traders bringing in supplies face extortion, looting, attacks, and even executions. "Sustained attacks, obstruction of aid and targeting of critical infrastructure demonstrate a deliberate strategy to break the civilian population through hunger, fear, and exhaustion." Despite repeated calls from humanitarian actors for all armed parties to the conflict to uphold their obligations under International Humanitarian Law and allow civilians in Al Fasher access to critical humanitarian assistance, civilians remain trapped under siege and face imminent risk of mass atrocities.

a1899.speaker: INGOs (joint statement)
a1899.speech: "It is imperative that warring parties distinguish between civilian gathering sites and infrastructure - including hospitals, water tanks, places of worship and markets - from military targets, and to refrain from using weapons that risk indiscriminate harm to civilians, including drones. Parties must guarantee safe exit and passage out of the city for those that wish to leave, and allow life-saving aid and commodities to enter. Humanitarian workers and assets must not be targeted, and Parties must provide concrete guarantees for their safety."

a1899.speaker: INGOs (joint statement)
a1899.speech: "As world leaders convene in New York this week, we call on the UN Security Council and its member states, including those supporting Parties to the conflict, regional actors including the African Union, and donor governments, to act on our plea for concrete, monitored action to protect civilians in Al Fasher. This includes securing protection for civilians along escape routes leading out of the city and in areas of destination. Particular attention must be given to the specific risks faced by women, and young men. Parties must also facilitate the sustained influx of humanitarian and commercial supplies, with strong guarantees for the protection of humanitarian workers - including local responders, traders, and aid assets."

a2009.speaker: Botswana Network on Ethics, Law and HIV/AIDS (BONELA)
a2009.speech: Has called for free condom distribution in prisons and public schools to prevent HIV and teenage pregnancies ; is advocating for policy changes that will ensure that students can access prevention services, and through the national human rights technical working group hopes to advise the government on necessary shifts to improve HIV/AIDS prevention.

a2009.speaker: Cindy Kelemi, Executive Director of BONELA
a2009.speech: Says reported cases show that sexual activities are common in prisons and in public schools.

a2009.speaker: Cindy Kelemi, Executive Director of BONELA
a2009.speech: Commended Botswana’s efforts to meet the UNAIDS target of 95/95/95 that aims for widespread HIV awareness and treatment, noting that while the country is currently at 95/98/98, it still falls short in reaching 100%.

a2009.speaker: Cindy Kelemi, Executive Director of BONELA
a2009.speech: Stressed the importance of providing prevention services, including condoms, especially within prisons, saying there have been cases where prisoners entered HIV-negative but left HIV-positive ; speaking in an interview, she expressed hope that the new government will prioritise prison health, particularly in HIV prevention, given its human rights-focused agenda.

a2009.speaker: Cindy Kelemi, Executive Director of BONELA
a2009.speech: Noted that, while the previous government cited laws against same-gender sex, the relevant section of the Penal Code was struck down by the courts in a landmark Letsweletse Motshidiemang vs Attorney General case where it concluded that there was breach of the fundamental right to privacy.

a2009.speaker: Cindy Kelemi, Executive Director of BONELA
a2009.speech: Calling for better access to condoms in public schools, especially in the face of rising teenage pregnancies, she said the alarming number of school dropouts due to pregnancy is a clear sign that students are engaging in unprotected sex.

a2009.speaker: Cindy Kelemi, Executive Director of BONELA
a2009.speech: Dismissed the recent US embargo on African countries, including Botswana, as an excuse for not providing condoms in prisons and schools. She emphasised that providing these services is essential to achieving comprehensive HIV prevention.

a2009.speaker: BONELA (report submitted to government)
a2009.speech: BONELA has submitted a report to the Assistant Minister of Justice and Correctional Services, Augustine Nyatanga, recommending access to condoms in prison.

a2014.speaker: Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations
a2014.speech: Announced the appointment of Coumba D. Sow to the post of United Nations Resident Coordinator in Togo, effective since 5 October 2024, an appointment approved by the Togolese government.

a2014.speaker: United Nations note/statement received by APA
a2014.speech: Notes that Ms Sow, originally from Senegal, brings 20 years of rich experience in development and humanitarian aid to this crucial post and that her career illustrates a deep commitment to development issues in Africa and beyond ; the document notes that her role as coordinator for emergencies and resilience for West Africa and the Sahel enabled her to develop valuable expertise in crisis management and the strengthening of regional resilience, and that her strategic post as head of Africa within the FAO Director-General’s Office gave her a global perspective on the challenges of agricultural and rural development across the continent.

a2080.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Minister of Health of Malawi (foreword to the Health Sector Strategic Plan)
a2080.speech: Says the HSSP III has placed communities at the heart of service provision through the reform on integrated platforms of care that will aim to achieve holistic and client focused care.

a2080.speaker: Twaibu Ali, Principal economist in the Ministry of Health of Malawi
a2080.speech: Said the implementation of the strategy comes at a critical time when Malawi's donors are freezing aid and population continues rising amidst free healthcare services ; said against this background, the ministry came up with a National Health Financing Strategy, which according to Ali, is already facing challenges.

a2080.speaker: Twaibu Ali, Principal economist in the Ministry of Health of Malawi
a2080.speech: Said Malawi needs to make a strong decision whether to continue with free health services or charge a cost to the services ; said among others the fund would mobilise resources through earmarked taxes like levies on beer, tobacco; private sector engagement; having voluntary health insurance and having optional paying services.

a2080.speaker: Malawi Health Sector Strategic Plan (HSSP III) (document)
a2080.speech: Indicative funding gap by pillar in 2022-2023 financial year shows that the ministry needs at least $1.8 billion (K3.151 trillion); the plan outlines the objectives, strategies and activities needed to build upon progress during implementation of the HSSP III and accelerate Malawi's progress in achieving Universal Coverage targets by 2030.

a2080.speaker: National Health Financing Strategy, Ministry of Health of Malawi (document)
a2080.speech: Says the ministry has to contend with drug shortages, poor equipment and infrastructure, high vacancies rates, lack of digital solutions and poor living conditions of Malawians; other challenges include aid freeze by the development partners; development partners reluctance to use a simple pool; political decision on establishment of a health fund; defining conditions for free access of health services which remains politically sensitive; weak regulations to support health financing reforms and institutional gaps in the public finance management ; states that of the 21 million people in Malawi, 71 percent live below poverty line, 84 percent live in rural areas, and that there is a high prevalence of diseases with 50 percent being preventable ones; life expectancy in Malawi is at 64 years; while Malawi promotes free healthcare, 55 percent of financing comes from development partners.

a2083.speaker: Kisu Simwaka, Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi (Facebook post)
a2083.speech: Posted on his official Facebook account on July 14 that the country's inflation "continues to descend slowly, reaching 27.1% in June 2025 - supported by softening food prices" ; "Non-food inflation edged down to 20.1%, from 22% in January 2024," adding that "while inflation has been decelerating in recent months, it remains high" ; "High inflation affects everyone, but is especially painful for lower-income households that spend a larger share of their income on food, housing, transport and other necessities. But the good news is that the overall inflation environment is improving - the continued decline in inflation has opened potential policy space to reduce interest rates. At its upcoming meetings, the Monetary Policy Committee will assess progress based on the totality of the incoming data, the evolving inflation outlook and balance of risks. Based on this assessment, they will decide whether to reduce or hold the policy rate constant, while waiting for further data."

a2083.speaker: National Statistical Office (NSO) of Malawi (data)
a2083.speech: Data quoted by Simwaka indicates that inflation has fallen from its peak of 35% in January 2024 while food inflation - "which accounts for more than half of the country's inflation basket - dropped to 31.6% from 44.9% in January 2024".

a2083.speaker: Kisu Simwaka, Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2083.speech: Indicated that the RBM's monetary policy "primarily looks at inflationary pressures coming from the demand side of the economy [and that] beyond monetary policy, it is important to realise that in a country like ours, inflation is affected by supply-side shocks"; "For instance, food prices are the major driver of the recent high inflation, but all countries face these shocks and have different inflation rates. We have an opportunity to achieve permanently lower inflation and therefore permanently lower interest rates. Effective supply-side responses should help to keep food price pressures in check. There is need for an urgent action to tackle supply-side constraints to increase production. Improved agricultural productivity is the most effective way of addressing food shortages. This underscores the importance of partnership between relevant stakeholder institutions in addressing the challenges of inflation. Such partnership should involve regular consultations, sharing information and strategies geared towards seeking solutions to supply constraints or challenges to food production and distribution with the overall objective of price stability. That should form the basis for long-term policy on domestic prices and food security."

a2083.speaker: Bertha Chikadza, economic analyst (interview with Malawi News Agency)
a2083.speech: Noted that this trend is encouraging, offering a glimmer of hope, especially regarding food prices: "This indicates that food prices are easing thanks to post-harvest supply improvements, especially in maize and legumes. It also reflects the positive outcomes of a tight monetary policy that has remained vigilant in the face of rising inflation." ; added that for the average Malawian, "this provides a breather, as the rate of price increases has slowed for four consecutive months, meaning the cost of basic necessities, particularly food, has eased slightly."

a2083.speaker: Mavuto Bamusi, economic analyst
a2083.speech: Cautioned that the government must ensure it procures maize from farmers before they sell it to vendors, who often resell the same maize back to the public at inflated prices: "While this is good news, products need to be safeguarded. Traders should not exploit Malawians by purchasing food from them and selling it at inflated prices, as this could lead to a resurgence in food inflation."

a2083.speaker: Kisu Simwaka, Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2083.speech: On July 1 commented on the challenges of forex, acknowledging that over the past decades, Malawi has faced persistent forex shortages "primarily because our export earnings are insufficient to cover the import bill"; "We import a lot more than we export. Every year, we import goods valued at US$3 billion, but only export goods valued at US$1 billion. This implies that our export receipts only pay for one-third of our import bill, leaving the country to look for foreign currency elsewhere to fund the remaining import bill." ; listed imports including fuel (US$560 million), fertilisers (US$350 million) and other goods taking up 75% of the annual import bill, and exports relying on tobacco (US$545 million), sugar, tea and legumes representing about 80% of annual export earnings, with large unrecorded transactions including informal or illegal activities estimated at US$500 million ; observed that "given insufficient export earnings to fund our imports, we have increasingly relied on foreign aid flows, external borrowing, and financial derivatives like foreign currency swaps to pay for the remaining two-thirds of the import bill - However, these have been unstable, leading to significant drawdowns on our foreign exchange reserves. However, prospects are improving - ongoing investments in commercial agriculture, energy, mining, manufacturing and tourism sectors are expected to boost economic activities and increase export earnings."

a2083.speaker: Kisu Simwaka, Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2083.speech: Said "no single crop can replace tobacco in the country at moment. But a combination of crops and products can earn the country much more than tobacco"; added that the Greenbelt Initiative "has designated approximately 1 million hectares of land, located within 20km of the country's three lakes and 13 perennial rivers, as potentially suitable for irrigation agriculture, through investment by both local and foreign investors"; said such irrigation expansion would require about US$2 billion for initial infrastructure and close to US$300 million as annual recurrent costs, with the mega farm programme targeting a minimum of 175,000 hectares of land by 2028/29 and potential export earnings from kilombero rice of US$10 million to US$100 million and from legumes of US$400 million to US$1 billion per year.

a2083.speaker: Kisu Simwaka, Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2083.speech: Observed that mining is positioned to become the largest export sector within the next five years and that projects being undertaken require about 230 megawatts while EGENCO currently has a total installed generation capacity of 441.95 megawatts, with the 360 megawatts Mpatamanga project coming up; "Furthermore, there is the construction of 50 megawatts Nanjoki power plant in Salima; Golomoti 28.5 solar PV power project; Salima 75.6 megawatts solar power project; 21 megawatts solar power project in Nkhotakota. Furthermore, Malawi and Mozambique are seeking funding for the Songwe dam project, which has potential of generating 180 megawatts to be shared 90 megawatts apiece by the countries."

a2083.speaker: Kisu Simwaka, Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a2083.speech: Reported on manufacturing that "the process of establishing Special Economic Zones (SEZs) to fast-track industrialisation is underway. The SEZs and/or industrial parks have been established to attract export oriented investment in the manufacturing sector... The industrialisation will lead to value addition of our exports, and increased foreign exchange earnings."; said government has identified land at Dunduzu in Mzuzu (72 hectares), Area 55 in Lilongwe (417 hectares), and Matindi in Blantyre (130 hectares), and Chigumula in Blantyre (22.7 hectares); "With these developments, export of primary commodities should be a thing of the past. We should be able us to export textile instead of just cotton, cigarettes instead of tobacco, processed or parked fish instead of raw fish, leather instead of just hides, juice instead of raw mangoes or oranges, furniture in place of logs/wood."

a2158.speaker: Hailemariam Dessalegn, Ethiopian Prime Minister
a2158.speech: Recently said that the import of sugar will be continued until the shortage is alleviated ; in his latest press briefing the PM apologized to the general public for the incident and he promised that the government will continue importing.

a2159.speaker: Demographic and health surveys conducted in 2011 (statistics)
a2159.speech: According to the statistics, 1,500 women continue to die every year from complications of pregnancy or childbirth; each time a mother dies, her baby is 10 times more likely to die before the age of one month and 3 times more likely to die before reaching the age of 5.

a2159.speaker: Michael Raynor, United States Ambassador to Benin
a2159.speech: Said it is a project that "supports the efforts of the government of the Republic of Benin in the areas of family planning, prenatal care, deliveries and postnatal care in the public and private health sectors." He specified that in Africa a child belongs to the whole village, and as we are today in a global village, the American diplomat urged the members of the village to stop letting children and their mothers die, because the country's development needs each of its sons.

a2159.speaker: Olga Agbohoui Houinato, Director of Maternal and Child Health
a2159.speech: Said the launch of the project makes its implementation official and aims to inform health sector partners and the entire Beninese population of the additional contribution of the American people to accelerating the improvement of the health status of Beninese families, complementing interventions already in place.

a2159.speaker: Raphael Edou, Minister serving as acting Minister of Health of Benin
a2159.speech: Said the project works to strengthen the health system, the quality and availability of services in health facilities and at the level of community relays through the scaling up of the package of high-impact interventions defined by the Ministry of Health. He specified that this package of interventions, commonly called PIHI, is a set of services which, when implemented on a large scale, demonstrate a reduction in illness and death among mothers, newborns and children.

a2159.speaker: Ministers Marcel de Souza (Development) and Naomie Azaria (Family)
a2159.speech: Welcomed this United States initiative which helps to reduce infant mortality. They expressed the wish that the project be well conducted in order to help the country reach MDGs 4 and 5 by the time of the review.

a2311.speaker: Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, Egyptian President, and Pedro Sanchez, Spanish Prime Minister (joint declaration)
a2311.speech: issued a joint declaration on Euro-Mediterranean relations, in a context marked by unprecedented challenges, notably irregular migration from sub-Saharan Africa ; Egypt and Spain committed to strengthening their regional partnerships in areas of common interest such as trade and investment, transport, energy, migration, agriculture and fisheries, justice, security, and the promotion of intercultural dialogue.

a2311.speaker: Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, Egyptian President, and Pedro Sanchez, Spanish Prime Minister
a2311.speech: expressed their deep concern at the persistent tensions in the Middle East and the risks they represent for the region and beyond; they welcomed the establishment of a ceasefire in Gaza as well as the release of hostages and detainees ; both sides insisted on the need to make this truce permanent to allow the safe and large-scale delivery of humanitarian aid and the release of the remaining hostages, and reaffirmed their commitment to supporting the Palestinian Authority in providing basic services in Gaza and restoring security.

a2311.speaker: Spain (government of Pedro Sanchez)
a2311.speech: underlined Egypt's key role as mediator and guarantor of the ceasefire agreement.

a2311.speaker: Egypt and Spain (joint declaration)
a2311.speech: agreed to work together for the stabilisation of Lebanon and Syria, as well as for the process of reunifying Libya's military and security institutions, stressing the importance of political and security progress, including the total withdrawal of foreign forces and mercenaries ; reaffirmed their cooperation on food and water security, insisting on the crucial importance of transboundary water management in accordance with international law, and recalled their attachment to the stability of the continent, notably in the Sahel and the Horn of Africa ; agreed to preserve the security of international navigation in the Red Sea, a vital passage for world trade, given its direct impact on the Suez Canal and global supply chains.

a2311.speaker: Spain (government of Pedro Sanchez)
a2311.speech: welcomed Egypt's efforts in favour of Sudan's stability.

a2311.speaker: Egypt and Spain (joint declaration)
a2311.speech: insisted on the need to respect Sudan's unity and territorial integrity, as well as the preservation of its state institutions ; reaffirmed the importance of launching an inclusive political process, led and driven by Sudanese political and civil forces, without external interference, in order to respond to the democratic aspirations of the Sudanese people.

a2424.speaker: Volker Turk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a2424.speech: Expressed profound concerns at the ongoing violent escalation in eastern DRC caused by the ongoing Rwanda-backed M23 offensive, telling a Special Session of the Human Rights Council in Geneva: "If nothing is done, the worst may be yet to come, for the people of the eastern DRC, but also beyond the country's borders"; said that since 26 January nearly 3,000 people have been killed and 2,880 injured in attacks by the M23 and their allies "with heavy weapons used in populated areas, and intense fighting against the armed forces of the DRC and their allies."

a2424.speaker: Volker Turk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a2424.speech: Noted that two hospitals in Goma had been bombed on 27 January, killing and injuring multiple patients, including women and children, and that in a mass prison break at Muzenze Prison in Goma on the same day at least 165 female inmates were reportedly raped and most were later killed in a fire under unclear circumstances, citing the authorities ; "I am horrified by the spread of sexual violence, which has been an appalling feature of this conflict for a long time. This is likely to worsen in the current circumstances," adding that UN staff were now verifying multiple allegations of rape, gang rape and sexual slavery in eastern DRC's conflict zones.

a2424.speaker: Volker Turk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a2424.speech: Insisted on the need to understand the conflict's global political and economic links: "The population in the eastern DRC is suffering terribly, while many of the products we consume or use, such as mobile phones, are created using minerals from the east of the country. We are all implicated."

a2424.speaker: Draft resolution circulated before the Human Rights Council Special Session
a2424.speech: Condemned Rwanda's military support of the M23 armed group and called for both Rwanda and M23 to halt their advance and to allow lifesaving humanitarian access immediately.

a2424.speaker: Bintou Keita, Special Representative of the Secretary-General in the DRC and head of MONUSCO
a2424.speech: Told the Council that dead bodies still lie in the streets of Goma, which M23 fighters now control, and that the situation is "catastrophic" ; "While I am speaking, youth are being subjected to forced recruitments and human rights defenders, civil society actors and journalists have also become a major population at risk. MONUSCO continues to receive requests for individual protection from them as well as from judicial authorities under threat and at risk of reprisals from M23 in areas under its control." ; warned about the health risks linked to the ongoing fighting, "especially the resurgence of cholera and the high risk of Mpox, the sudden interruption of children's schooling, and the rise of conflict-related sexual violence and gender-based violence"; said medical personnel face electricity cuts and lack fuel for their generators for basic services, including morgues: "I again call on international community to advocate for humanitarian assistance to reach Goma immediately."

a2424.speaker: Patrick Muyaya Katembwe, DRC Minister of Communications and Media
a2424.speech: Spoke out against the continued logistical, military and financial support of countries including Rwanda "to armed groups operating on our territory"; maintained that Rwanda's support for the M23 had fuelled the violence in eastern DRC "for more than 30 years, exacerbating the war for reasons linked to the exploitation of the strategic mining resources of the Democratic Republic of Congo."

a2424.speaker: Ambassador James Ngango, Rwanda's Ambassador to the United Nations in Geneva
a2424.speech: Dismissing that claim, insisted that a large-scale attack against Rwanda was "imminent"; accused the "Kinshasa-backed coalition" of stockpiling a large number of weapons and military equipment near Rwanda's border, mostly in or around Goma airport: "These weapons include rockets, kamikaze drones, heavy artillery guns capable of shooting precisely within the Rwandan territory. The weapons were not turned at the theatre of operations against the M23, rather they were pointed directly at Rwanda."

a2956.speaker: Harry Kalaba, Citizens First (CF) leader
a2956.speech: Urged Zambian leaders to draw lessons from the U.S. democratic process, particularly in light of Donald Trump's inauguration as the 47th President of the United States; in a statement expressed his admiration for the U.S. political system, which he believes offers valuable lessons for Zambia and Africa at large: “The much-anticipated inauguration of Mr. Donald Trump as the 47th President of the United States tomorrow is a great lesson for Zambia and the rest of Africa as far as democracy is concerned”

a3052.speaker: Brian Shukan, United States Ambassador to Benin
a3052.speech: welcomed the bringing into use of the facility, the fruit of cooperation between Benin and the United States. "MCA-Benin II is the best symbol of the cooperation between Benin and the United States, which has lasted for 60 years," he declared.

a3052.speaker: Gabriel Degbegni, National Coordinator of MCA-Benin II
a3052.speech: said he is proud to take stock of the new infrastructure the country is benefiting from. "It is a source of pride for the staff of MCA-Benin II, who have overcome many challenges to achieve the objectives," he remarked.

a3052.speaker: Abdoulaye Bio Tchane, Minister of State for Development and Coordination of Government Action and Chairman of the Board of MCA-Benin II
a3052.speech: welcomed the implementation of MCA-Benin II, which impacts 12 million Beninese and opens prospects for Benin's economic development thanks to the availability of electricity. "The Compact is the best development financing tool," he confided.

a3072.speaker: Statista (September 2022 research report)
a3072.speech: Reported that the USA and China emerged as the top spenders on R&D activities, with US$680 billion and US$550 billion, respectively, and that the robust economic growth of most developed countries can be directly attributed to their substantial investments in basic and applied research and experimental development.

a3072.speaker: UNESCO Institute for Statistics
a3072.speech: Reports that global spending on R&D has surged to a record high of almost US$1.7 trillion.

a3072.speaker: Statista (2022 report)
a3072.speech: Reported that only 0.38 per cent of Ghana’s GDP is allocated to research and development.

a3278.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a3278.speech: Said nearly two dozen countries in Africa are already in or at high risk of debt distress.

a3278.speaker: Trevor Manuel, Chair of the Africa Expert Panel
a3278.speech: Told Reuters the panel had already begun to make detailed recommendations on improving the G20 Common Framework: "One of the reforms is that the opportunities in the Common Framework should be available to all middle-income countries as well."

a3278.speaker: Some analysts
a3278.speech: Believe Washington's withdrawal from multilateralism could leave a space for China to occupy, but it is unclear if Beijing aims to do that.

a3278.speaker: G20's financial stability watchdog (Financial Stability Board)
a3278.speech: Said on Monday it had developed a new plan to tackle climate risks but it had paused further policy work in light of the U.S. retreat from climate action.

a3278.speaker: Duncan Pieterse, Director General of the South African Treasury
a3278.speech: Said in a statement on Monday that he hoped to issue the first Communique under the South African G20 presidency at the end of the meetings.

a3360.speaker: Khumbudzo Ntshavheni, South African Minister in the Presidency
a3360.speech: Announced on Thursday at a press briefing after her Cabinet meeting the $115 million in PEPFAR funding, running six months from 1 October 2025 to 31 March 2026: "PEPFAR aims to guarantee the continuity of HIV services in South Africa by supporting service continuity and by giving priority to each country's specific needs and to their vital impact."

a3360.speaker: Khumbudzo Ntshavheni, South African Minister in the Presidency
a3360.speech: Stressed the importance of maintaining momentum towards South Africa's goal of reducing HIV prevalence to 0.1% by 2032, and called on the government and international partners to ensure that progress is not reversed: "We must not regress. We can achieve an HIV-free society later in this period."

a3366.speaker: Baimankay Sankoh, WFP's Deputy Country Director in Kenya
a3366.speech: "This generous rice contribution from the Republic of Korea is more vital than ever for WFP to continue supporting the food needs of hundreds of thousands of refugees." ; "Most refugees are unable to work or return home and are entirely dependent on humanitarian assistance to survive. We sincerely hope this expanded rice contribution will continue in the future." ; "Korean rice is known for its high quality. Its reliable, annual delivery allows WFP to plan effectively and respond flexibly to shifting needs on the ground. This predictable support safeguards the dignity of refugees by ensuring access to sufficient and nutritious food."

a3366.speaker: Baimankay Sankoh, WFP's Deputy Country Director in Kenya
a3366.speech: "WFP's operations supporting refugees in Kenya are under immense strain. With available resources stretched to their limits, we have had to make the difficult decision to again reduce food assistance. This will have a serious impact on vulnerable refugees, increasing the risk of hunger and malnutrition."

a3366.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a3366.speech: Said the support comes at a critical time, as WFP faces major funding shortfalls; in May the agency warned that refugees in Kenya are at risk of heightened food insecurity after it was forced to cut assistance to the lowest levels ever recorded.

a3366.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) (data)
a3366.speech: According to WFP, the Global Acute Malnutrition rate among refugee children and pregnant or breastfeeding women in Kenya is over 13 per cent—well above the emergency threshold of 10 per cent in refugee contexts.

a3366.speaker: Kang Hyung-shik, Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to Kenya
a3366.speech: Reaffirmed his country's commitment to humanitarian solidarity: "The Republic of Korea is proud to stand alongside other nations in responding to the rising hunger crisis and providing hope to thousands of families in the eastern Africa region. Our history is deeply rooted in global solidarity, and we remain committed to standing with those in need."

a3404.speaker: Utku Cakirozer, Turkish MP
a3404.speech: Questioned why Turkey was covering construction costs of the Somali embassy and what safeguards existed to prevent potential misuse of diplomatic property: "We are not only giving the land but also constructing the building. We don't know the cost, nor do we know who will build it. Shouldn't this be subject to stricter scrutiny?" He pressed for information on the procurement process and asked whether competitive bidding had taken place.

a3404.speaker: Utku Cakirozer, Turkish MP
a3404.speech: Questioned whether Somalia has reciprocated Turkish support on issues of importance to Ankara, including international recognition of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC): "We say this relationship is special, but has Somalia reciprocated in areas important to us?"

a3404.speaker: Yunus Emre, Turkish lawmaker
a3404.speech: Also expressed concern over accountability mechanisms.

a3404.speaker: Turkish Foreign Ministry officials
a3404.speech: Responded that the land could only be used for diplomatic purposes and that Turkey retains veto rights over any attempt to sell, rent, or repurpose the property; any disputes would be resolved amicably and outside international courts, which they said was standard practice for bilateral protocols of this kind.

a3404.speaker: Refik Ali Onaner, director general for North and East Africa at the Turkish Foreign Ministry
a3404.speech: Said in his testimony that the Somali embassy project is being funded entirely by the ministry's budget as a "gift" to Somalia - a symbolic act of friendship, and confirmed the Turkish government would fully cover architectural, construction, and outfitting costs.

a3404.speaker: Refik Ali Onaner, director general for North and East Africa at the Turkish Foreign Ministry
a3404.speech: Told lawmakers that total Turkish aid to Somalia since 2011 exceeds $1.15 billion, with approximately $850 million directed toward humanitarian and development projects and $300 million in military support, including a $3.5 million contribution toward Somalia's debt settlement with the International Monetary Fund, disbursed in December 2023.

a3404.speaker: Yilmaz, Turkish official
a3404.speech: Acknowledged the criticism but emphasized the deal's strategic utility: "This isn't a typical bilateral relationship. It's a relationship built on a strategic alliance, and it positions Turkey as a key actor in the stabilization of the Horn of Africa." He described the Mogadishu embassy as one of Turkey's largest diplomatic hubs worldwide, exceeding even many of its NATO and EU mission compounds.

a3404.speaker: Yilmaz, Turkish official
a3404.speech: Said the Anatolia Barracks in Mogadishu, the Turkish military's largest overseas base, which has trained more than 15,000 Somali troops since 2017, plays a key role in Somalia's fight against al-Shabab.

a3404.speaker: United Nations Panel of Experts (2022 report)
a3404.speech: Concluded that Turkey had violated the international arms embargo on Somalia by delivering Bayraktar TB2 drones on December 6, 2021, flown in aboard Turkish military Airbus A400M aircraft, and that the Turkish government failed to seek the required Security Council exemption.

a3404.speaker: Critics on the Turkish parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee
a3404.speech: Citing reporting by Turkish media, warned that official development assistance may be disproportionately benefiting firms close to Erdogan, alleging that under the guise of aid, contracts are being funnelled to politically connected companies with business operations in Somalia.

a3404.speaker: Turkish Foreign Ministry figures
a3404.speech: According to ministry figures, bilateral trade fell from $426 million in 2023 to $384 million in 2024.

a3404.speaker: Derya Bakbak, Turkish ruling party MP
a3404.speech: Argued that Somalia's trust in Turkey stems from Ankara's clean record, untainted by colonialism: "Wherever Turkey goes, it brings justice, development and sincerity," describing the partnership as a symbol of Turkey's vision to become a global power.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: Opening remarks: "The year 2024 saw profound changes in the international landscape as well as remarkable progress in China's reform and development. Under the stewardship of General Secretary Xi Jinping, China made important progress in its diplomacy." Said China fostered a good external environment for high-quality development, brought much-needed stability to a changing and turbulent world, and made new strides in building a community with a shared future for mankind; said that this year the international situation is still full of challenges but the mission of China's diplomacy remains unchanged.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On head-of-state diplomacy: said it is "the highest form of China's diplomacy", citing the three monumental events China hosted (the 70th anniversary of the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence, the FOCAC Beijing Summit and the China-Arab States Cooperation Forum), President Xi's four overseas visits and over 130 diplomatic engagements; said China's foreign policies are increasingly welcomed, China's role in addressing global challenges increasingly commended, and the Chinese path to modernization increasingly emulated; announced 2025 highlights including the 80th anniversary commemoration of the victory in the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the SCO summit.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On China-Russia relations: "no matter how the international landscape evolves, the historical logic of China-Russia friendship will not change and its internal driving force will not diminish" ; said the two countries have found a path of "non-alliance, non-confrontation and not targeting any third party", and that a mature, resilient and stable China-Russia relationship "will not be swayed by any turn of events, let alone be subject to interference by any third party. It is a constant in a turbulent world rather than a variable in geopolitical games" ; said the two sides will use the joint commemoration of the 80th anniversary of the victory in WWII to advocate the correct historical view, defend its victorious outcomes and uphold the U.N.-centered international system.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On China's global role in 2025: said "we are living in a changing and turbulent world, where certainty is becoming a scarce resource" and that China's diplomacy "will stand firm on the right side of history" and "provide certainty to this uncertain world"; said China will be a staunch force defending national interests — "We never provoke, and we are not intimidated by provocations. No maximum pressure, threat or blackmail can undermine the unity of the 1.4 billion Chinese people" — a just force for world peace and stability, a progressive force for international fairness and justice, and a constructive force for common development.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On Trump's "America First" policy and U.S. withdrawal from international organizations (in response to CNN): "There are more than 190 countries in the world. Should everyone stress 'my country first' and obsess over a position of strength, the law of the jungle would reign the world again. Smaller and weaker countries would bear the brunt first, and international norms and order would take a body blow." Said a big country "should honor its international obligations and fulfill its due responsibilities. It should not put selfish interests before principles, still less wield its power to bully the weak"; said over 100 countries support China's Global Development, Global Security and Global Civilization Initiatives and more than three quarters of countries have joined Belt and Road cooperation.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On the Global South: said the Global South accounts for over 40 percent of global GDP and contributes as much as 80 percent of global growth and "holds the key to bringing stability to the world"; urged that the Global South strengthen themselves, stand together in unity and strive for development, noting Indonesia's BRICS membership and the SCO, BRICS and G20 summits to be hosted by China, Brazil and South Africa; said "China is naturally a member of the Global South" and "our heart will always be with the Global South".

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On the Ukraine crisis and U.S.-Russia talks: said China has been calling for political settlement through dialogue and negotiation since the first day of the crisis, released a position paper, sent a special representative for shuttle diplomacy and initiated the Group of Friends for Peace at the U.N. with Brazil and other Global South countries; said "China welcomes and supports all efforts for peace", that "No one wins in a conflict, but everyone gains in peace", and that China is ready to continue to play its constructive role; said security should be mutual and equal and no country should build its security on the insecurity of another.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On China-U.S. science and technology competition and DeepSeek: said "where there is blockade, there is breakthrough; where there is suppression, there is innovation", that "'small yard, high fence' cannot suppress the spirit of innovation, and decoupling and supply chains disruption will only lead to self-isolation", and that science and technology "should not be used to put up an iron curtain"; cited the Global AI Governance Initiative, the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All, and the Initiative on International Cooperation in Open Science proposed with Brazil, South Africa and the African Union.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On the Trump administration, tariffs and fentanyl: said "No country should fantasize that it can suppress China and maintain good relations with China at the same time. Such two-faced acts are not good for the stability of bilateral relations"; said China scheduled all fentanyl-related substances in 2019 at U.S. request but the abuse of fentanyl "is a problem that must be confronted and resolved by the United States itself" and the U.S. "should not return good with evil, or even impose arbitrary tariffs"; said "China will definitely take countermeasures in response to arbitrary pressure", and that China will stay committed to Xi Jinping's three principles of mutual respect, peaceful coexistence and win-win cooperation.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On the Shanghai Cooperation Organization: said this year is the SCO's "China Year", that the SCO has grown over 24 years from six members to a big family of 26 countries, that China as rotating president is putting together more than 100 events under the slogan "Upholding the Shanghai Spirit: SCO on the Move", and that China will host the SCO summit in Tianjin this autumn.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On the United Nations and the international order: said "the more complex the problems, the greater the need to accentuate the important status of the U.N."; called for cementing the cornerstone of sovereign equality — "Those with stronger arms and bigger fists should not be allowed to call the shots" — upholding fairness and justice, observing multilateralism, and strengthening the authority of the international rule of law; said China is a founder, beneficiary, advocate and builder of the post-WWII order with "no intention to start all over again", nor does it support any country's attempt to overturn the current order.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On the U.S. plan to "take over" and "own" Gaza: said "Gaza belongs to the Palestinian people. It is an inseparable part of the Palestinian territory. Changing its status by forceful means will not bring about peace, but only new chaos"; said China supports the plan for restoring peace in Gaza initiated by Egypt and other Arab countries and that if some major country truly cares about the people in Gaza "it should promote comprehensive and lasting ceasefire, ramp up humanitarian assistance, observe the principle of Palestinians governing Palestine, and contribute to the reconstruction in Gaza"; called for more support for the two-State solution and independent statehood for Palestine.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On China-Africa relations and FOCAC (in response to News Agency of Nigeria): said China and Africa are "always good friends, good partners and good brothers with a shared future" and the relationship "is now at its best in history"; said China has helped Africa build or upgrade nearly 100,000 kilometers of roads and more than 10,000 kilometers of railways, Chinese enterprises created more than 1.1 million new jobs in Africa in the past three years, and China has remained Africa's largest trading partner for 16 consecutive years; said "There will be no global modernization without African modernization" and that China stands ready to deliver on the ten partnership actions, including zero-tariff treatment for 100 percent tariff lines and 1,000 "small and beautiful" livelihood projects, and firmly supports South Africa's G20 presidency.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On U.N. General Assembly Resolution 2758 and Taiwan: said the Western narrative that the resolution is not equivalent to the one-China principle is "a blatant challenge to the authority of the U.N. and the post-WWII international order. It is extremely absurd and dangerous"; said Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory, that Resolution 2758 "precluded any possibility of creating 'two Chinas' or 'one China, one Taiwan'", that "Taiwan is never a country, not in the past, and never in the future", and that "China will realize reunification, and this is unstoppable".

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On neighborhood diplomacy and U.S. mid-range missile deployment: said China has reached common understanding on building a community with a shared future with 17 neighboring countries, signed Belt and Road cooperation agreements with 25 countries in the neighborhood and remains the largest trading partner of 18 of them; said China is "firmly opposed" to U.S. deployment of mid-range capability missile systems in the region, that years after the U.S. released its "Indo-Pacific Strategy" it has done "Nothing, except for stirring up troubles and creating disputes", and that "Asia is not an arena for big power rivalry. It should become a demonstration field for international cooperation".

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On China-EU relations: said this year marks the 50th anniversary of China-EU diplomatic ties, that bilateral trade has expanded from US$2.4 billion to US$780 billion and investment from almost zero to close to US$260 billion; said China and the EU jointly make up over one-third of the world economy, that "China remains confident in Europe and believes Europe can be our trustworthy partner", and that the two sides have the capacity and wisdom to properly resolve pending issues through friendly consultation.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On global public opinion toward China: said "Friendship between the people is the foundation for bilateral relations and motivation for peace"; confirmed that people in the Global South view China positively because "China has always engaged with other developing countries with sincerity and good faith"; said that among people from developed countries "discovering and embracing China has become a trend", and urged people to "get rid of the information cocoon and take off the tinted glasses".

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On China-Japan relations: said leaders reached important common understandings last November on building a constructive and stable China-Japan relationship fit for the new era and that bilateral relations have demonstrated a momentum of improvement; said Japanese militarists "committed heinous crimes to the people in China and all over Asia" and that "Guarding against the revival of militarism is a duty Japan must carry out without a moment's relaxation"; warned unrepentant individuals in Japan working with "Taiwan independence" forces to "Stop the propaganda that 'a Taiwan emergency is a Japanese emergency'", because "to provoke trouble in the name of Taiwan is to invite trouble for Japan".

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On Latin America and U.S. pressure: said China's cooperation with Latin American and Caribbean countries is South-South cooperation with "only mutual support in this cooperation, no geopolitical calculations", and that China "never seeks sphere of influence or targets any party"; said "What people in LAC countries want is to build their own home, not to become someone's backyard; what they aspire to is independence and self-decision, not the Monroe Doctrine"; announced China will host the Fourth Ministerial Meeting of the China-CELAC Forum in the first half of this year.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On the Chinese economy: said the Chinese economy registered five-percent growth last year "amid unilateral sanctions and suppression from the United States and others", and that confidence comes from China's super-sized market, robust industries, innovative drive and institutional strength; said China has granted unilateral visa-free entry to 38 countries and extended the transit visa-free period to 240 hours for 54 countries, and will work for a better business environment, cut down the negative list, lower the threshold of market access and continue unilateral opening up to the least developed countries.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On the South China Sea and the Code of Conduct: said the South China Sea maintained peace and stability last year and remained the safest and busiest waters for international navigation; said an official from a regional country noted the Philippine moves to create frictions are like a "shadow play", adding that "For every move on the sea by the Philippines, there is a screenplay written by external forces, the show is livestreamed by Western media, and the plot is invariably to smear China"; said China will continue to safeguard its territorial sovereignty in accordance with law, that "infringement and provocation will backfire and those acting as others' chess pieces are bound to be discarded", and that the third reading of the COC text has been completed.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On the 30th anniversary of the Fourth World Conference on Women: said China will convene a Global Leaders' Meeting on Women in the latter half of this year as a follow-up to President Xi's proposal; said China has upheld gender equality as a basic state policy, supported the work of U.N. Women, partnered with UNESCO on the Prize for Girls' and Women's Education, helped fellow developing countries implement 100 maternal and child health projects, and trained over 200,000 female professionals for more than 180 countries and regions.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On China-India relations: said the meeting between President Xi and Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Kazan last October provided strategic guidance for improving bilateral ties; said "A cooperative pas de deux of the dragon and the elephant is the only right choice for both sides", that the two should never allow bilateral relations to be defined by the boundary question, and that as important members of the Global South they have the responsibility to take the lead in opposing hegemonism and power politics.

a3450.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a3450.speech: On consular protection of Chinese nationals overseas: said that in 2024 China safely evacuated more than 10,000 Chinese citizens from Lebanon, Haiti and other high-risk areas, processed more than 50,000 consular protection cases, handled over 500,000 calls on the 12308 hotline and issued more than 5,000 safety alerts — "No matter where you are, the motherland will never be far"; said the telecom fraud parks in northern Myanmar near the border with China have all been removed and China has joined forces with Thailand, Myanmar and Laos in the Thailand-Myanmar border region; outlined three priorities for 2025 to strengthen the safety protection system for Chinese nationals overseas.

a3516.speaker: action medeor (German non-governmental organisation) — terms of reference / call for proposals
a3516.speech: States that access to medicines is part of the human right to health, yet an estimated 2 billion people worldwide still face major obstacles preventing them from obtaining and using the treatments they need, and that “the recent elimination of USAID funding has only exacerbated the situation”; regions affected by emergencies, disasters and crises have even more difficulty guaranteeing access for their populations. In order to support innovative and sustainable responses to these challenges, action medeor is launching a call for proposals to support short-term, small-scale pilot projects testing new approaches to improving access to essential medicines in humanitarian or disaster-affected contexts, with a maximum project amount of 70,000 EUR, open to non-profit organisations officially registered in Burundi, with a submission deadline of 25 August 2025.

a3516.speaker: WHO/MSH framework on access to medicines (2000)
a3516.speech: Describes four dimensions of access: availability, accessibility, affordability and acceptability.

a3516.speaker: Recent research
a3516.speech: Continues to highlight a series of persistent obstacles across these dimensions of access, such as the lack of research on relevant treatment options, the instability of supply chains, the prohibitive cost of medicines for patients and low levels of health literacy or trust in available treatments.

a3631.speaker: Local processors in Mali
a3631.speech: Welcome the decision taken by the authorities to temporarily suspend the export of certain oilseed products in the country.

a3631.speaker: Kancou Keita Cissé, director of Mali-Shi
